subject: IP indemnity carve-in vs carve-out — proposed split and evidence staging
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: IP indemnity carve-in questions and redline

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement & legal at Aurora asked me to push a few open items on the Order Form / MSA redlines before we proceed to signature. High level ask: we need clearer language on who carries IP risk when Aurora data or customer prompts are involved (i.e., output infringement risk). Currently our legal team is seeing the indemnity as ambiguous and wants a carve-in for third-party IP claims tied to Aurora-originated training/signals.

Two concrete asks from Aurora Legal (attached redlines):
- Carve-in request for any third-party claim that alleges infringement arising from Aurora data or fine-tunes we provide.
- A stronger evidence-and-notice protocol (we need timelines & a single evidence custodian).

We realize this is sensitive for Redwood re: defend vs. reimburse and control of defense. We are open to a technical evidence staging approach (escrow or limited retention) but Aurora wants minimal operational burden.

Attached: aurora_redlines.pdf (highlighted in blue).

Can you run this with your legal and procurement and propose a narrow compromise? We are on a tight procurement window — would like to reach agreement this week if possible.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Strategic Procurement | Aurora Analytics
[Attachment: aurora_redlines.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IP indemnity carve-in questions and redline

Ellen —

Appreciate the clear framing and the redlines. I looped in Kimberly (legal) and Jordan (account lead) so we can respond with a proposed compromise and an operational plan. High-level suggestion from our side:

Proposed split (compromise):
- Carve-in limited to claims that allege infringement directly tied to Aurora-supplied training data or clearly reproducible prompts provided by Aurora (i.e., provable input->output linkage).
- Standard carve-out for general model hallucination outputs or third-party content that predates Aurora inputs.
- Defense allocation: Redwood will offer to defend (right-to-defend) claims within the carve-in, but we request joint control for strategic decisions with defined fallback (Aurora reserves right to step in if material conflict).
- Cap: align indemnity exposure to the Order Form MRR x 12 (or mutually agreed cap) for carve-in claims.

Operational / evidence staging:
- We can accept an evidence staging approach: Aurora provides a minimal evidentiary bundle (input artifacts, timestamps, and outcome artifacts). Redwood will store that bundle in a short-term escrow (90 days) for triage; longer-term escrow only if litigation opens.
- Single custodian: we propose Aurora names a single evidence owner; Redwood names a single ops liaison.

I attached a tracked redline from Redwood for quick review. Kimberly — can you review the defend/control language and the cap math? Jordan — if we can land this commercially, Aurora is ready to sign the order form after legal confirms.

Timeline: if we get legal alignment today we can route a DocuSign by tomorrow.

Thanks —
Priyom
Head of Enterprise GTM | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_Redwood_track.pdf (PDF, 34KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: comment on Aurora carve-in proposal

Priyom / Jordan —

Quick thoughts after reading Aurora's redlines + your counter (Priyom). I ran this against our standard MSA playbook and flagged a few items. Summary below and inline comments in the attached internal_playbook.docx.

Key legal positions we should push to preserve risk profile:
- Narrow the carve-in trigger: require demonstrable linkage (hashes, original prompt + model response with timestamped logs). Weak causal allegations should remain carved out.
- Right-to-defend: we are willing to defend but need unilateral control of litigation strategy for efficiency. We can offer joint consultation for settlement decisions above a de minimis threshold (e.g., > $50k) with a defined escalation path to execs.
- Cap sizing: Order Form MRR x 12 is acceptable as a starting point but add an exception for willful misconduct or gross negligence.
- Evidence retention: 90-day staging by default, extendable to 365 days if Aurora requests and pays associated storage & legal hold costs.

Operational asks to include in the redline: who pays for preservation costs, ticketing flow for evidence requests, and a named technical contact. Those reduce ops surprises.

I left suggested language that I think Aurora will accept (I kept the spirit of your compromise). If you want, I can draft a digest email to Ellen that frames the compromise as a path-to-signature (short bullets + next steps).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal_playbook.docx (DOCX, 120KB)]

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aurora Analytics Legal <legal@aurora-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-08-19T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IP indemnity carve-in questions and redline

Priyom / Kimberly —

Thanks — that compromise language looks reasonable to Aurora Legal with the clarified linkage and the 90-day staging approach. A few quick confirmations:
- Aurora will name our evidence custodian (Legal Ops) and will include the minimal artifacts you described.
- We accept the cap tied to annualized MRR with the willful-misconduct carve-out retained.
- Regarding defense control: Aurora's preference is joint consultation but we can accept Redwood-led defense provided Redwood commits to a 3-business-day notice before material settlement decisions.

I'll circulate a final annotated redline from Aurora Legal this morning; once Kimberly confirms the defend/settlement notice language we can accept and I will route DocuSign for the Order Form (link below).

DocuSign (Order Form): https://www.docusign.com/aurora/AUR-2028-0032-orderform

We appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to hop on a 20-min call if there are any last clarifying points.

Best,
Ellen
Director, Strategic Procurement | Aurora Analytics
[Attachment: aurora_final_comments.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]
